title: Relative Brauer group and Galois second cohomology via crossed products
author_responsibility: Original statement and proof by J.S. Milne. The author attribution to Tate (1976, 5.2) is preserved.
material_provenance: Editorial TeX checked against the fixed original author PDF, with original page and offset locators retained.
difficulty_reason: Milne constructs the crossed product from the factor set and establishes its relative Brauer class. For multiplication, he builds an explicit balanced tensor bimodule carrying the summed factor set, then identifies its endomorphism algebra by dimensions and the simple-module structure.

statement: Complete original finite Galois relative Brauer-group isomorphism
proof: Original bijection and full Lemma 3.15 balanced tensor multiplication proof, including attribution
Original relative setup, factor set, classification statement and basis proof
Original inverse construction, simplicity by minimal support and change of cocycle
context: Original splitting and equal-dimension representative criterion

dedup.scope: CFT II.3.11 (900008205) is an all-degree Tate cohomology shift for class formations. CFT VII.8.1 (900008207) relates global reciprocity to local invariants. Neither classifies all relative Brauer classes of finite Galois splitting fields or proves the crossed-product group law. Other current SQL crossed-product hits concerned operator algebras or bicrossed Hopf products.

readability.basis: Selected author statement, proof and context directly compared with the fixed original PDF. All four compiled reader pages inspected.

source_caveats: The proof preserves the original finite Galois range. The author calls Lemma 3.15 a sketch and cites Blanchard and Farb–Dennis. The actual source supplies the balanced tensor space, both actions, the induced homomorphism and dimension and matrix identifications. A targeted independent review confirmed that the remaining action checks use standard algebraic identities.
